newsitem.title: USA: Conn. atty genl seeks U.S. Internet gambling ban.
newsitem.headline: Conn. atty genl seeks U.S. Internet gambling ban.

text.p: Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal on Wednesday urged passage of a federal law to clearly ban gambling on the Internet.
Blumenthal and other state attorneys general appeared before a U.S. Senate subcommittee on Wednesday to back legislation they said was essential to preserve state regulation of gambling.

"Gambling and the Internet is a mix that is a recipe for deceit and financial disaster," Blumenthal said in a statement. "This legislation would clarify existing law and explicitly ban any gambling communication -- including Internet communications -- not authorized and regulated by the states."

The proposal would give state attorneys general the power to go to court to block Internet gambling and provide fines of up to $10,000 and two years in prison for those who operate Internet gambling enterprises.
It would also provide fines of up to $5,000 and one year in prison for those who use the gambling service.
Blumenthal said the proposal, introduced by U.S. Sen. John Kyl of Arizona, would allow states to continue to regulate all gambling within their borders.
